body.statement: For a polynomial covariance parametrization \(\phi_G\) over a field of characteristic zero, if the generic rank of its Jacobian is strictly smaller than \(|\theta_G|\), then the generic fiber of \(\phi_G\) has positive dimension; in particular, \(\phi_G\) is not generically finite-to-one.

source.locator: Section 3 discussion of the Jacobian-rank nonidentifiability argument and Section 7.1 generic-fiber computations
source.verbatim_statement: By Lemma 2 in the supplement, it is sufficient to show that, under the conditions of the theorem, J does not have generically full column rank. A mixed graph G is generically infinite-to-one if and only if ID(G) = infinity; in that case the fiber is generically of positive dimension.

attestation.note: Verified against Foygel, Draisma, and Drton, arXiv:1107.5552v2, proof of Theorem 2 and Definition 7; the two quoted source passages jointly carry the Jacobian-rank-to-positive-dimensional-fiber implication used here.
